# Appendix B: Extended Methods {.unnumbered}

::: {.callout-note}
This appendix documents the corrected analytical design, not the
invalidated pre-fix estimates. Numeric examples tied to the older
velocity-positive narrative have been removed until all manuscript tables
are regenerated from the cleaned pipeline.
:::

## B.1 Survival Framework

The primary design remains a survival analysis of time to program
completion. The key outcome is whether a grantee-disaster program reaches
the completion threshold within the observed reporting window, with
right-censoring for programs still active at the end of observation.

The baseline specification is a Cox proportional hazards model:

$$
h(t \mid \mathbf{X}) = h_0(t)\exp(\mathbf{X}\boldsymbol{\beta})
$$

where $h(t \mid \mathbf{X})$ is the completion hazard at quarter $t$,
$h_0(t)$ is the baseline hazard, and $\boldsymbol{\beta}$ captures the
association between covariates and completion timing.

Hazard ratios are interpreted conventionally:

- HR > 1 implies a higher completion hazard
- HR < 1 implies a lower completion hazard
- HR = 1 implies no detectable association

## B.2 Quarter-Based Temporal Construction

The corrected workflow defines elapsed time using unique
grantee-disaster-quarter observations rather than activity-row counts.
This matters because the raw standardized QPR file can contain many rows
within the same quarter. Treating row counts as duration creates
pseudo-time and can mechanically distort:

- observed duration
- phase assignment
- early-window feature construction
- time-varying survival reshaping

All active downstream features now depend on a quarterly panel produced
before phase and window calculations are applied.

## B.3 Time-Varying Covariates

The active analysis emphasizes time-varying survival models because
spending pace changes over a program's life. Velocity and related process
measures are therefore allowed to vary by quarter rather than being
collapsed immediately to one static summary.

The manuscript treats these time-varying specifications as primary. Static
summaries and alternative windows remain useful diagnostics, but they are
secondary to the corrected quarter-based panel.

## B.4 Phase And Window Features

Lifecycle analyses remain part of the design, but all phase definitions
must be quarter-based. Conceptually, the workflow partitions each program
into early, middle, and late periods based on corrected elapsed quarters.
Any claims about lifecycle differences are provisional until regenerated
tables from the cleaned pipeline are inserted into the manuscript.

Early-window features are also defined on unique quarters. This change
eliminates the earlier bug in which "first N quarters" could silently mean
"first N activity rows."

## B.5 Heterogeneity Strategy

Subgroup analyses are still used to examine whether capacity proxies behave
differently across contexts such as disaster type, program type, and
grantee experience. In the current manuscript posture, these analyses are
exploratory rather than confirmatory.

That posture reflects two practical constraints:

- subgroup sample sizes are limited
- the project is still reconciling regenerated diagnostics and manuscript
  tables after the quarter-based correction

## B.6 Sensitivity Analyses

The active workflow continues to assess robustness through:

- alternative completion thresholds
- alternative feature definitions
- diagnostic comparisons between static and time-varying specifications
- subgroup and interaction checks

Only rerun results that agree with the corrected pipeline will be promoted
into the main text.
